newsitem.title: UK: Blue Circle wins 6.0 mln stg damages.
newsitem.headline: Blue Circle wins 6.0 mln stg damages.

text.p: British cement manufacturer Blue Circle Plc was awarded six million stg in contamination damages from the Atomic Weapons Establishment (AWE), London's High Court said on Tuesday.

Blue Circle had sued AWE, part of the Ministry of Defence, after one of its ponds containing radioactive water burst following floods, and contaminated part of Blue Circle's estate at Aldermaston in Berkshire.
The estate included offices and a 34-bedroom conference centre.
Despite an evacuation exercise, the land contained plutonium content way above normal levels.
A Blue Circle deal to sell the estate for 10 million stg fell through three-and-a-half years after the floods.

The cement firm accused the MOD of not revealing details of the contamination. Justice Carnwath ruled on Tuesday that the MOD must take the blame for the pollution which resulted in a major land blight for its neighbours.

Justice Carnwath ruled that he had no doubt that sale of the site to U.S.-based Sun Microsystems Ltd got aborted due to the pollution leak which took place in 1989. "The 1989 incident resulted in levels of radioactivity well above the normal background levels and above the regulatory threshold," he said.
The judge said he had awarded five million stg on the basis of what he considered the site would be worth after it had been cleared and another million as interest.
The MOD will also have to pay an estimated 500,000 stg in legal costs.
